function.name: search_by_content
function.description: Search notes by full-text content. Use for topic or keyword searches when you don't know the exact note title. Returns up to 10 notes ranked by relevance. For multi-faceted queries, call this alongside other tools and intersect the results yourself.

query.description: Text to search for in note content. Use specific topic keywords (e.g. 'gradient descent', 'BERT', 'docker'). Do NOT use category words like 'meeting notes' or 'research notes' — use search_by_tags for that.

function.name: search_by_tags
function.description: Search notes by tags using AND logic — only notes matching ALL listed tags are returned. Use for category-based queries. Common tags: meeting, journal, reference, project, deep-learning, nlp, transformer, attention, python. Use 1–2 tags maximum; more tags narrow results aggressively and may return nothing.

tags.description: List of tags (lowercase). All must match. Examples: ["meeting"], ["project"], ["nlp", "python"], ["attention"].

function.name: search_by_date
function.description: Search notes by creation date range. For a single-day query, set both date_from and date_to to the same date. Returns all notes created within the range.

date_to.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). For a single day, use the same value as date_from.

function.name: get_note_by_path
function.description: Retrieve the full content of a note using its exact file path. Use this when you already know the path from a previous tool result. Path format must include the folder: 'research/Transformers.md', 'projects/Paper_Recommender.md'.

path.description: Full file path including folder, e.g. 'research/Transformers.md' or 'meetings/Advisor_Meeting_Jan10.md'.

function.name: get_note_by_title
function.description: Retrieve the full content of a note by its title. Title is the filename without .md extension, with underscores replaced by spaces. Examples: 'Transformers', 'Self Attention', 'CNN Architecture', 'Paper Recommender'. Do NOT add words like 'project', 'the', or 'research' to the title. If not found, use search_by_content to discover the correct title.

title.description: Note title — filename without .md, underscores as spaces. Must be exact. Examples: 'Transformers', 'Python Tips', 'Reinforcement Learning', 'Chatbot Prototype'.

function.name: get_outgoing_links
function.description: Find all notes that a given note links TO using wiki-style [[links]]. Use for queries like 'what does X reference?', 'what are the prerequisites of X?', 'what topics does X build upon?'. Requires the exact file path of the source note.

path.description: Full file path of the source note, e.g. 'research/Transformers.md'. If you only know the title, first call get_note_by_title to retrieve the path.

function.name: get_incoming_links
function.description: Find all notes that link TO a given note (backlinks). Use for queries like 'what notes reference X?', 'what links to X?', 'what is connected to X?'. Takes the note title, not a path.

title.description: Title of the target note — filename without .md, underscores as spaces. Examples: 'Transformers', 'Attention Mechanisms', 'Paper Recommender'. Do NOT include folder or file extension.

function.name: get_vault_stats
function.description: Get statistics about the vault: total note count, folder breakdown, and tag counts. Use when the user asks about vault structure or overview.

function.name: get_recent_notes
function.description: Get the most recently modified notes. Use when the user asks about recent activity, or to discover note titles when unsure of exact names.

limit.description: Number of recent notes to return (default 10).

function.name: create_note
function.description: Create a new markdown note in the vault. Use when the user asks to write, create, or synthesize a new note. The note is immediately searchable after creation. Use get_note_by_title or search_by_content first to gather relevant content from existing notes before writing.

title.description: Title of the new note. Use Title Case with spaces (e.g. 'Attention Survey', 'Project Status'). Do not include .md extension.

folder.description: Destination folder. Must be one of: research, projects, meetings, daily, reference.

content.description: Markdown body of the note. May include headings, lists, and wiki-style [[links]] to other notes.

tags.description: List of lowercase tags, e.g. ['research', 'deep-learning'] or ['meeting', 'advisor'].
